title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced a single shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the same candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced structured workflow policies and could trigger at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We revise the manuscript to (1) give a compact formal definition of the binary scoring rule used for the confirmatory test, (2) add a concise nearest-work comparison matrix contrasting key design choices, (3) tighten introduction and interpretation of the shared-generation design trade-off, and (4) move provenance detail into a compact archival-reference paragraph while preserving deterministic execution facts and reproducibility pointers.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into concrete network configuration commands, potentially improving NetOps productivity. However, syntactically plausible commands can violate workflow invariants (for example, changing MTU without an enforced shutdown or performing hazardous uplink switchover), producing semantic failures only visible in closed-loop execution. Prior work therefore recommends integrating verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before enactment (see Related Work). Evaluating guarded pipelines requires executable tests that detect stateful and sequencing errors beyond token- or syntax-level correctness.

This study asks a narrowly scoped confirmatory question, preregistered before execution: Does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To isolate validator/repair effects we used a shared-initial-candidate paired design: for each task we generated one candidate (shared) and scored that identical candidate under both the baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (validator±repair) conditions. This design removes generator-induced variance across paired episodes and cleanly measures the marginal effect of a validator and bounded repair policy. A known trade-off of this choice (explicit in the preregistration) is that if the generator systematically produces valid candidates for the chosen task bank, the guard will be idle and cannot improve outcomes—an interpretation we make explicit in Results and Discussion.
sections.related_work:
Two research strands frame our study. First, executable/emulation-grounded NetOps benchmarks and verification tools demonstrate that text-level correctness does not guarantee safe enactment: closed-loop emulation exposes sequencing and stateful errors—make-before-break mistakes, group-availability violations, and required-ordered operations—that token-level checks miss (representative benchmark/tool reports include arXiv:2608.23179, arXiv:2604.22513, and related executable-benchmark work). Second, tool-augmented LLM-agent and bounded-autonomy architectures (veto layers, canaries, generate→validate→repair pipelines, translation-to-formal-model approaches) are repeatedly proposed as operational safety measures (survey and position reports summarized in the archived bibliography).

Nearest-work comparison (compact). We summarize closest prior experimental/benchmark efforts and mark core design axes relevant to interpreting our contribution. For each cited work we indicate: whether it uses an executable/emulation test harness (Exec?), whether the experiment isolates validator marginal effects with a shared-generation paired design (SharedGen?), whether it includes an explicit bounded repair budget (Repair≤1?), whether the task corpus is synthetic/deterministic (Synthetic?), and whether the study exercises multiple generator models (MultiModel?). Entries below are compacted from the verified evidence records cited in our archive.
- NetConfArena (arXiv:2608.23179): Exec = yes; SharedGen = no; Repair≤1 = varies; Synthetic = yes; MultiModel = limited.
- Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair (arXiv:2604.22513): Exec = yes; SharedGen = no; Repair≤1 = no (benchmarked repair methods); Synthetic = yes; MultiModel = limited.
- Aether (arXiv:2604.18233): Exec = yes (digital-twin style); SharedGen = no; Repair≤1 = no; Synthetic = testbed/emulation-focused.

Where prior work focused on generator-centered evaluation or multi-model leaderboards, our methodological contribution differs: we hold the generator fixed and use a paired shared-candidate design to isolate whether an executable validator and a bounded repair policy change outcomes for identical generated outputs. This isolates a complementary causal question to generator-focused studies (generator-error rates) and highlights experimental trade-offs for future confirmatory protocols.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) before execution. Key preregistered elements (copied verbatim in archived preregistration) include: paired-binary confirmatory design with N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, primary test = exact two-sided McNemar, and bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Exclusions, contamination rules, repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic reset controls, and sensitivity analyses were prespecified.

Task generation, model, and harness. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task manifest contains intent, required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), initial_state, expected_final_state, and difficulty metadata. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini; execution accounting records model_calls_used = 120 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 120}. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) executed in an emulator that enforces structured workflow policies (for example: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break). The preregistered repair policy allowed up to one repair iteration per guarded episode when validator.violation_count > 0.

Formal binary outcome definition (compact and explicit). The confirmatory paired binary label for each pair was derived deterministically from archived scorer and validator outputs as follows:
- PASS (binary = 1) if scorer.score == 1 AND scorer.score_reason_code == "VALID_CONFIGURATION" AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true AND validator_trace.violation_count == 0.
- FAIL (binary = 0) otherwise (for example, any validator.violation_count > 0 or scorer.score != 1). Repair activity in a guarded episode is indicated by validator_trace.repair_applied == true and archived repair_provider_trace artifacts.

Concrete archived example illustrating a PASS (archived artifact). execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json shows: normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer; score = 1; score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION"; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; validator_trace.violation_count = 0; hence binary = PASS per the above rule. Concrete archived FAIL example: none exist in the archived scoring artifacts because every scored episode in both conditions met PASS (see Results). This absence is reported directly rather than invented.

Statistical procedures. Primary confirmatory test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired PASS/FAIL labels with reported exact p-value. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI for the paired-difference estimate computed by resampling paired outcomes (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) as prespecified. Sensitivity analyses and multiplicity controls are described in the preregistration but are either vacuous or exploratory given the observed outcomes (no exclusions, no repairs).
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. The run completed according to the preregistered stopping rule with no technical exclusions: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition-level summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes.

Per-topology counts (prespecified partition). The deterministic task partition produced 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology results from archived scoring artifacts are:
- Edge (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Core (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Leaf–spine (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.

Representative diagnostic artifact. Representative scoring artifact execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (archived) shows: normalized_response equals normalized_reference_answer; parsed_command_count equals required_command_count; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; validator_trace.repair_applied = false; scorer_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; scorer_version = 5.0. These representative traces illustrate the pass decision logic and confirm that repair was not invoked for that pair.

Repair incidence and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 for every guarded episode, repair_applied = false across the run and no repair_provider_trace artifacts were generated. Thus preregistered secondary endpoints quantifying repair incidence and repair-call counts are empirically zero in this run and are reported as such.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and linkage to the shared-generation design. The preregistered shared-generation paired design isolates the marginal effect of an executable validator and bounded repair policy by scoring identical generated outputs under both conditions. In this archived task bank and under the declared generator/prompt configuration the shared initial candidates satisfied the deterministic emulator validator in all 120 pairs; consequently the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair behavior and could not reduce semantic failures relative to the baseline. The observed exact McNemar p = 1.0 and degenerate bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00] are statistical expressions of this ceiling result and directly reflect the preregistered design choices and archived outcomes.

Design trade-offs and concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations. The shared-generation protocol increases internal validity for isolating validator effects but may under-exercise repair when the generator is well-calibrated for the chosen task bank. Based on archived task-manifest difficulty metadata (fields: dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level) and the recorded absence of repairs we recommend the following preregistered design adjustments for future confirmatory runs intended to measure repair utility:
1) Independent generation per condition: allow separate generator draws per condition so guarded pipelines can intercept generator errors that arise from prompt or sampling variability; preserve blocking or stratification to control confounding where needed.
2) Controlled prompt perturbations: apply systematic, preregistered prompt perturbations to a subset of tasks to increase generator error incidence while keeping other blocks paired for internal controls (the preregistration included exploratory perturbation variants that archived task metadata permit selecting).
3) Targeted task stratification: concentrate confirmatory power on tasks labeled 'very_hard' or with high dependency_rule_count in the manifest to increase probability of generator-induced violations and exercise repair.
4) Exploratory expansion of repair budget: allow multiple repair iterations in exploratory arms to observe repair convergence behavior and repair-call costs.

Threats to validity (brief). Internal validity: strong—deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audit logs, zero exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity: limited by the validator's policy encodings derived from synthetic task payloads; the validator enforces required_sequence checks but does not simulate all vendor-specific subtleties or partial-observability telemetry. External validity: constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40 and targeted absolute reduction 0.15; observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions and renders the confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and illustrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear if generators sometimes produce invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we provide an artifact-rich, preregistered paired protocol and deterministic archival traces (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) that enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. The archived artifacts permit follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and evaluate more production-rooted corpora to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
